items.headline: HIV prevention drug rollout expands to reach 3 million more people
items.summary: The U.S. State Department and the Global Fund announced they will rapidly scale up access to lenacapavir, a twice-yearly injectable that prevents HIV, aiming to reach three million people in lower-income countries over the next three years. That is a fifty percent increase over previous commitments for this near-perfectly effective prevention shot.
items.why_it_matters: Wider access to a long-acting HIV prevention shot could meaningfully accelerate progress toward ending the HIV epidemic in the hardest-hit countries.
